summary: Verified score 7.0/10. Odrum is not on par: the score is under 7.5. There is no blocker, and three majors are confirmed (M1 splashes, M2 icon black eye recesses, M3 ult and cast pose snaps). All five minors are kept. The build is unchanged: hashes for odrum.glb (208d570f), icon (8d8066fe) and the three splashes (f44a7a70, 4354af5f, 65b0c069) match the reviewer's. Card mtimes are Nov 5, and the GLB (Nov 6 19:51) predates the clip_steps report (Nov 8 00:09). I tried to refute M3 as a sampling artefact. A glTF parse shows cast_ult and cast_a1 baked at 1/30 s keys with LINEAR interpolation, so the head and pot jumps are real pose cuts between adjacent keys. I viewed the base and Noon Fair splashes at full size: the eyeball-like raised pot and the lost yoke on Noon Fair are real. I made upscaled icon views (128 px and a 48 px downsample): the slits are near-black, against odrum.md:85. In the match frame the diagonal yoke with two pots reads well, and the ochre mask block and grey-oat cap are correct. That in-game strength holds the score at 7 despite weak cards. Sensitivity: the cap is a low dome with a nub, not a hood. The mask keeps its brow band, nose keel and cheek planes at 48 px, so it reads stern, not horror, hockey mask or mannequin. The icon is the closest item to that line and is covered by M2. Shadeprint follows ruling 2. No blocker was missed. Leftover correction: 'golden-ochre diluted' is partly (fixed in game, open on the cards), not fixed. Timing not measured (load ~4).

findings.title: All three splashes are brush-filtered model cut-outs; on the base card the raised pot reads as an eyeball
findings.what: splash.png, odrum_noon_fair_splash.png and odrum_shadeprint_splash.png are the in-game model, posterize-filtered and pasted on a blurred painted plate. Base: the raised pot is the largest shape on the card, a pale sphere with one dark end-on disc that reads as an eyeball beside a pale scowling plate. Noon Fair: one pot shows, the bar collapses onto the shoulder, and the figure is pushed into the right third.
findings.evidence: Viewed art/out/fighters/odrum/splash.png (sha f44a7a70) and odrum_noon_fair_splash.png (sha 4354af5f) at full size in this pass; both mtime Nov 5 00:13-00:14, unchanged. Earlier crops: _harness/_shots/closing_odrum_verify_splash_head.png, closing_odrum_splash_toppot.png.
findings.gauge: LoL splashes are painted illustrations: the signature prop reads at a glance, value and rim light structure the figure, and each skin has its own composed moment. VALE's cards are filtered 3D cut-outs with no paint-over.
findings.fix: Stage each card from Odrum's own kit (base: the Amber Hour lob with the yoke as a long diagonal and both pots in three-quarter view; Noon Fair: a festival porter pose with both pots on the bar; Shadeprint: a dusk silhouette keyed by the amber inlays). Drop the posterize pass, paint over face, prop edges and rim light, grade the mask to the in-game ochre #EFC88F, re-run card_qa.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed by viewing. Hashes match the reviewer's. The eyeball read on the base card is real, and Noon Fair loses the yoke. It stays a major, not a blocker: the eyeball is a prop read, not a face.

findings.title: Icon eye recesses are black holes; the 128 px chip reads as a hollow-eyed scowl
findings.what: In icon.png the almond recesses drop to near-black (right eye p50 L* 2.0). The brief requires umber-ink walls of L* ~30 to ~21 floor and 'never black holes'. With the pale cracked plate and the hard brow slant, the most-seen face in the HUD reads menacing. The portrait (512 px) keeps L* ~23, so the fault is the icon's light, not the paint.
findings.evidence: icon.png sha 8d8066fe (Nov 5 00:16), unchanged. _harness/_reports/closing_odrum_c3_icon_eyes.txt: box 66,57,8,3 p50 L* 2.0 min 1.4; box 37,57,6,3 p50 13.0. Upscaled views made in this pass: _harness/_shots/closing_odrum_v2_icon_x4.png and closing_odrum_v2_icon48_x4.png (48 px downsample, x4). Brief: _design/fighters/odrum.md:85. Precedent: owner ruling 2.
findings.gauge: LoL face chips of masked champions keep a readable, alive eye area at 48-64 px. The eyes are the focal point, never a void.
findings.fix: Re-light the icon camera only: add a warm low bounce from the pot side so recess walls hold L* 25-30 and the floor stays at or above 18, add a small amber glint per recess, soften the brow tilt a few degrees. Check at 48, 64 and 128 px.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. The black slits are against the brief's own rule (odrum.md:85). Checked for a blocker: at 48 and 128 px the mask still shows a brow band, nose keel, cheek planes, warm ochre and the felt cap, so it reads as a stern carved mask, not horror, hockey mask or mannequin. It stays a major, but it is the one item closest to the sensitivity line.

findings.title: Ult and casts snap the head and pots between consecutive keys
findings.what: cast_ult: head 0.377 m and x_pot_l 1.902 m in one 60 Hz step at clip f17.5-18. cast_a1: head 0.185 m, x_pot_l 1.157 m. cast_a3: head 0.165 m. attack2 x_pot_l 0.923 m. The GLB bakes these clips at 30 fps keys with LINEAR interpolation (cast_ult has 44 keys, integer frames 14-22 all present), so the pose change happens between two adjacent 30 fps keys. That is a pose cut, not a sampling artefact.
findings.evidence: _harness/_reports/closing_odrum_c3_clip_steps.txt (Nov 8 00:09, after the GLB mtime Nov 6 19:51; odrum.glb sha 208d570f). In this pass a python glTF parse of the cast_ult/cast_a1 samplers confirmed 1-frame key spacing and LINEAR interpolation. The game plays the clip by role: src/render/actors.ts:121.
findings.gauge: LoL ultimates whip fast along continuous arcs, using anticipation, smear frames or trails. The head never jumps position between frames, least of all on the signature cast.
findings.fix: Re-key the cast_ult release (f16-19) so the torso and head rotate over at least 3 keys, carry the speed with a held anticipation and an amber resin smear on the pot path, and do the same on cast_a1 f9-12, cast_a3 f8 and attack2 f5. Re-apply the death clip_lift afterwards. Gate: head at or under 0.1 m per 60 Hz frame.
findings.verifierNote: Tried to refute it as a sampling artefact. Refuted that idea: keys are 1/30 s apart with linear interpolation, so the 0.75 m head move between keys f17 and f18 is real. Major is right for the showcase ability. A 19 px head pop and a ~95 px pot pop at 1080p are visible even under VFX.

findings.what: The cap, chest and skirt sit in the road's hue family (hue 24-36 vs road 33). Odrum separates by value only.
findings.gauge: A LoL champion keeps a signature hue that reads on any lane tile.
findings.fix: Widen the resin amber a little: a lampresin band on each pot's shoulder and a resin-stained hem, within the accent budget.
findings.verifierNote: Kept. The yoke and pots still carry the silhouette in the frame.
